floating_point: x87 FPU, not SSE. Retail uses fld dword/qword/xword (80-bit extended) and stores through fstp; control-word handling is native x87.
implications: Numeric comparison must use x87 80-bit extended semantics, not double-precision SSE.
FP natives (FP_InitExtendedPrecision, FP_SetDefaultPrecision, FP_MergeControlWord, FP_*ControlWord*) depend on the x87 control word and must be compared on that basis.
Candidate x86 builds default to the same x87 unit, so the same control word applies to both sides.
